newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel moves against Palestinians after bombing.
newsitem.headline: Israel moves against Palestinians after bombing.

text.p: Israel suspended peace talks over a Jerusalem suicide attack, made arrests and threatened to re-enter Palestinian areas to seize "terrorists" on Thursday if President Yasser Arafat's forces failed to do the job.
Arafat's aide said the moves were "a declaration of war against the (Palestinian) Authority and against the Palestinian people".
"And instead of fighting terror they decided to fight the Palestinian Authority," Arafat aide Nabil Abu Rdainah told Israel's Channel Two Television.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet demanded Arafat clamp down on Moslem militants responsible for double suicide bombings that killed 13 people and wounded 170 at a Jerusalem market on Wednesday.
"I think the Palestinian Authority has had a very free ride. Basically the line was what they do is okay and the obstacle to peace is on this side," Netanyahu told Reuters in an interview.
He accused Arafat of having done "damn all" to tackle violence and said the international community had an obligation to demand action from the Palestinian leader.

"I believe that peace can move forward only if the Palestinian Authority and Yasser Arafat undertakes what he hasn't done so far and that is a full court press against the terrorists. They must live up to their obligations," he said.
Israeli and Palestinian security forces arrested alleged Moslem militants in separate raids in the West Bank and Gaza.

The Israeli army said its forces had detained 28 Palestinians overnight in connection with "hostile terrorist activities". It gave no details of the raids, staged in Palestinian villages still under Israeli occupation.

Palestinian security officials said they had arrested at least 10 activists of the militant Islamic Jihad and Hamas movements in the PLO-ruled Bethlehem area. They said they made arrests in other areas under their control but gave no details.
In the Gaza's Khan Younis, PLO forces arrested Dr Abdel Aziz Rantisi, a Hamas political leader, his brother said.
Netanyahu said Israel would arrest Arafat's police chief Ghazi Jabali, accused by Israel of organising attacks on Jewish settlers, if he left PLO territory. Jabali rejected the charges.
Officials said Israeli-PLO security meetings took place late on Wednesday in the West Bank but they did not elaborate.

A leaflet issued in Hamas's name claimed responsibility for Wednesday's attack. Israeli pathologists were trying to identify the bodies of the two bombers. An Israeli official briefing said the Hamas leaflet "seems authentic but we are not sure".

At Dahariyeh village near the West Bank city of Hebron, Israeli forces detained members of two Palestinian families whose two sons, both Islamic militants, have been missing for 15 months, relatives said. It was not immediately clear if the missing pair were the two suicide bombers.
In Jerusalem, mourners streamed to cemeteries for the funerals of victims of the deadliest attack on Israelis in over a year. Memorial candles flickered at the market.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said U.S. President Bill Clinton's top Middle East advisers planned to meet later on Thursday to assess the status of the peace process but they were unlikely to present any recommendations.

In the West Bank town of Ramallah, the 88-member Palestinian Legislative Council added to pressures on Arafat by giving him one month to dissolve his cabinet and appoint a new one following a corruption probe.
Late on Wednesday, Netanyahu's security cabinet ordered a halt to peace moves and vowed to act.

"The cabinet decision is quite clear. If Israel has to, that is if the Palestinian Authority is not going to do what it is supposed to do against the terrorists, Israel will have to do it," Netanyahu's adviser David Bar-Illan told Reuters.
"Israel will have to go into the areas controlled by the Palestinian Authority if that is necessary and get the terrorists there," he said.

Israel sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip immediately after the Jerusalem attack. Military checkpoints blocked movements of residents and tourists alike. Israel prevented Palestinian newspapers from being delivered to self-ruled Gaza.

PLO officials said Israel's confiscation of lands and expansion of Jewish settlements had caused Palestinians despair and frustration. Peace talks have been stuck since March, when Netanyahu broke ground on a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Abu Rdainah insisted the Palestinian Authority was preventing attacks from being launched from areas under its control and warned Israel against "overstepping the red line" by entering Palestinian-controlled territory.
World leaders urged Israel and the Palestinians to press on with talks but U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross postponed a planned mission to salvage peacemaking to allow mourning.
